verdict.rationale: Smithery documents its own REST interface for connecting to MCP servers, API-key-scoped management of namespace resources, and a CLI for searching the registry, adding connections and calling tools, so a real programmatic surface exists. Nothing claims parity with the UI, the documented publishing flow reads as UI-driven, and probes found no OpenAPI spec. missing for 10: an explicit API/UI parity statement, documented API coverage of publishing and server management, a published OpenAPI or full API reference, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Smithery gives you a simple REST interface for connecting to MCP servers.
Resources within a namespace can be managed by anyone with the appropriate API key scoped to that namespace
smithery mcp add <url>                  # Add an MCP server connection
smithery tool call <connection> <tool> [args]  # Call a tool
